status: CLOSED for the two rows that can be pressed at all — `;` and `'` are now proven by real key events in a PACKAGED build, twice. The standing item from slices 19, 20, 21, 22 and 29 is resolved as far as a keypress can resolve it.
theStandingItem: Slice 19 re-homed ten video.* registrations onto VideoCoreStudyOverlay and fixed effectiveKeys to normalize. Slices 19, 20 and 21 each recorded that nobody had pressed a key; slice 22 pressed R/W/S and recorded that the rows which do NOT seek were still unpressed, because its instrument is a `seeked` event. Slice 29 wrote the phase for them and could not run it.

howThisGotUnblocked.problem: slice 29's phase H sits behind phase E in a DEV-route harness, and phase E regressed under another session's concurrent edits to the working tree. Re-running it would keep measuring a tree nobody has a stable picture of.
howThisGotUnblocked.solution: move the phase to the PACKAGED harness. A packaged artifact is frozen at build time and does not move when the working tree does; a dev-route harness re-reads the tree on every run. The build used here is the same 09:28 artifact that passed all six phases twice in slice 27, unchanged.
howThisGotUnblocked.generalLesson: when the tree is unstable, a frozen artifact is not merely an acceptable substitute for a dev run — it is the only route whose result means anything. This is worth reaching for the next time slice 21's hazard recurs.

whatThisProves: The full keyboard path for these two rows in a real packaged build: window keydown -> chordFromEvent -> effectiveKeys normalization -> chordMatches -> the handler stack -> VideoCoreStudyOverlay's changeSubtitleDelay -> the rendered offset. Slice 22 proved that path for the three rows that seek; this proves it for the two that move the subtitle delay, which is a different handler and a different observable.
theControl: `x` was pressed last and the offset did not move. Without it, two deltas would prove only that SOMETHING moves the delay while keys are being pressed. `x` is free in BOTH the catalog and the adopted player's own vc_defaultKeybindings — the distinction slice 22 paid for when it first used `q` and got a seek to 0.

twoInstrumentTrapsPaidFor.notDataTimingDelay: `data-timing-delay` looks like the obvious seam and is not: it lives on the drift-tracking section and only renders while `driftTracking && timingDrift`. A phase built on it reads null in an ordinary run and looks like a broken shortcut rather than a missing instrument.
twoInstrumentTrapsPaidFor.textShapeNotAriaLabel: the offset `<output>` is matched by text shape (/^[+-]?\d+(\.\d+)?s$/), not by its aria-label, because every label here goes through useT() and this app ships four UI languages. A selector keyed to English would pass on an English machine and fail after a language switch.
twoInstrumentTrapsPaidFor.punctuationKeys: `;` and `'` are not letters, so the `Key${K}` code and letter VK table that phase G of the dev harness uses do not describe them. A wrong code/VK pair dispatches happily and matches nothing — which reads exactly like 'the binding does not fire'. Semicolon/186 and Quote/222 are set explicitly.
twoInstrumentTrapsPaidFor.whereTheControlsLive: the subtitle-offset cluster is in the `study-control-primary` row, NOT behind the `toggle-study-controls` expander — so no expansion step is needed, and a phase that adds one is testing the expander instead.

whatRemains: Five rows — subEarlierLarge, subLaterLarge, toggleAutoPause, toggleLoop, toggleFurigana — ship with defaultKeys: ''. effectiveKeys returns '' and chordMatches is false for EVERY chord, so they are unpressable by design until a user binds them. 'Press them' is the wrong test and no harness work will make that keypress exist. The untested claim for those five is bind-then-press through ShortcutSettings (Settings -> Shortcuts does expose the Video category), which needs a settings-driving phase no harness currently has. This is a statement about what the rows ARE, not a deferral.
